references.authors: Rao SV, O'Donoghue ML, Ruel M, Rab T, Tamis-Holland JE, Alexander JH, et al.
references.claim: Monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages are key cellular populations linking acute necrosis, inflammatory clearance, and tissue repair. After myocardial infarction, monocytes undergo state transitions from acute inflammation-driven programs toward recovery and remodeling-biased states.
references.contribution: This proposal tests whether an intervention-associated transcript response depends on macrophage-fibroblast context, which is a different question from the monocyte state transitions described in this work.
references.limitation: This work does not establish a context-dependent transcript response to a specific intervention in macrophage-fibroblast coculture.
references.title: Peripheral blood transcriptomes and a single-cell atlas suggest a monocyte-associated immune recovery-failure axis in STEMI

references.authors: Liu T, Liu Y, Liu Y, Wen D, Sun J, Zhang Y, Gao Y, Zheng D
references.claim: Extracellular vesicles in wound healing and scar formation are regulated by macrophages, fibroblasts, and their crosstalk. These cells undergo state transitions from acute inflammation-driven programs toward recovery and remodeling-biased states.
references.contribution: This proposal tests whether an intervention-associated transcript response depends on macrophage-fibroblast context, which is a different question from the extracellular vesicle regulation described in this work.
references.limitation: This work does not establish a context-dependent transcript response to a specific intervention in macrophage-fibroblast coculture.
references.title: Extracellular vesicles in wound healing and scar formation: molecular regulation of macrophages, fibroblasts, and their crosstalk

references.authors: Mao L, Zhou D, Zhou G, Lu X
references.claim: m6A methylation regulatory network in pulmonary fibrosis: Molecular mechanisms from RNA stability to cellular phenotype transition. m6A modification is not a uniform pro-fibrotic or anti-fibrotic switch, but rather a dynamic regulatory network that links RNA metabolism to PF progression and therapeutic opportunities.
references.contribution: This proposal tests whether an intervention-associated transcript response depends on macrophage-fibroblast context, which is a different question from the m6A methylation regulation described in this work.
references.limitation: This work does not establish a context-dependent transcript response to a specific intervention in macrophage-fibroblast coculture.
references.title: m6A methylation regulatory network in pulmonary fibrosis: Molecular mechanisms from RNA stability to cellular phenotype transition (Review)
